description: The graph illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percentage) of various methods—Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME—across different co-occurrence numbers, with the x-axis representing the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale ranging from $10^1$ to $10^3$, and the y-axis showing accuracy from 60% to 85%. Each method is represented by a distinct line: Base (black, solid), FT (blue, dashed), IKE (red, dash-dotted), MEND (brown, dotted), MEMIT (purple, dash-dot), and ROME (green, solid). All methods show an increasing trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases. At $10^1$, the Base method starts at approximately 66%, FT at 67%, IKE at 69%, MEND at 72%, MEMIT at 71%, and ROME at 76%. By $10^3$, the Base method reaches about 82%, FT reaches 81%, IKE reaches 82%, MEND reaches 84%, MEMIT reaches 83%, and ROME reaches 85%. The ROME method consistently achieves the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence numbers, while the Base method consistently has the lowest accuracy.
